title: Everything was gone…
paragraphs:
Everything was gone…
in a single day.

Children.
Wealth.
Security.
Future.

And the man who lost it all…
did something nobody expected.
He worshiped.
The messengers kept coming.
One breathless report after another.

Raiders stole the oxen.
Fire from heaven burned the sheep.
Camels taken.
Servants killed.
Then the final blow.
A house collapsed.

All ten of Job’s children…
gone.

No time to process.
No time to prepare.
Just devastation.

Job tore his robe.
He shaved his head.
The ancient language of grief.
Then he fell to the ground.

Not in rage.
Not in curses.
In worship.
And these words thundered through the ashes:

“Naked I came from my mother’s womb,
and naked I shall return.
The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away;
blessed be the name of the LORD.”
— Job 1:21
Faith does not mean you feel no pain.
Job’s heart was shattered.
But he knew something deeper than loss.

Everything we hold…
was never ours to begin with.

Children.
Money.
Health.
Breath.
All gifts.
And the Giver is still good—even when the gift is gone.
Some scholars interpret the opening of Job as a heavenly courtroom scene showing that suffering can occur without being punishment for personal sin.
Job was not being crushed for wickedness.
He was being witnessed by heaven.

A man who loved God
even when the blessings disappeared.
But the Book of Job whispers a deeper prophecy.
Another innocent man would suffer.

Not just lose children—
but become the Son who was crushed.

At the cross,
Jesus Christ lost everything.

Friends fled.
Body broken.
Blood poured out.
So that when we lose everything…
we do not lose God.
Because the cross proved something forever:
God is not distant from suffering.
He entered it.
He carried it.
And He defeated it through the resurrection.
If you are in a season where life feels stripped bare…
remember Job’s whisper in the ashes:
“The LORD gave.”
And the Lord who gives…
also restores.
And remember:

Jesus is still worthy—
even in the ashes.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
